access.edition_or_version: English translation by Jayant Karve and Eleanor Zelliot (Calcutta, 1984)

mechanics.premise: A Brahmin outsider rises to police chief of Pune by serving a minister's appetite for control, then is destroyed by the same power once he becomes inconvenient.
mechanics.point_of_view: Dramatic; no single narrator, but the chorus and the machinery of power frame events.
mechanics.style_and_devices: Uses song, folk-theatre (tamasha) forms, and a chorus against an unflinching account of political instrumentality and caste violence; the historical setting carries a satirical charge aimed at contemporary politics.
mechanics.emotional_progression: Desire for status -> complicity -> degradation -> collective destruction, without redemption.
mechanics.dialogue: Public and performative; private integrity is largely unavailable to the characters.
mechanics.setting: Eighteenth-century Peshwa Pune, staged through folk performance conventions.
mechanics.critical_reception: A landmark of modern Indian theatre; first performed 16 December 1972 in Pune; Jabbar Patel's 1973 production is considered a classic. Translated into English in 1984.
mechanics.verification_note: Existence, date, authorship, translator, and premise confirmed via Wikipedia 'Ghashiram Kotwal' API extract. Described only; no text reproduced. Translation limits: Marathi folk and caste idiom do not fully transfer into English.
